extracted.intended_audience: comedy fans, travelers, and people looking for notable comedy venues in California (including aspiring performers)
extracted.subtask_description: A travel-style listicle identifying and describing notable comedy clubs across California, highlighting what makes each venue worth visiting (history, performers, programming, amenities). Useful for visitors and locals deciding where to see or perform comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prestige / celebrity performers hosted
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the club has hosted famous, high-profile comedians or notable events (e.g., 'served as the location for Dave Chappelle’s return to comedy', 'Countless famous comedians have performed at The Comedy Store').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs that have been the stage for well-known comedians or landmark performances are presented as more noteworthy. Examples on the page: The Laugh Factory (Dave Chappelle), The Comedy Store (countless famous comedians).

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical legacy / founding year
rubrics_metrics.description: The venue's age and historical significance (the page lists 'Founded in' dates like 1972, 1974, 1978, 1982, 2008, 2013).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Older venues with longstanding histories (e.g., founded in the 1970s or 1980s) are framed as institutions with established reputations; founding year is used as an implicit signal of credibility and legacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reputation and community support
rubrics_metrics.description: Local and industry reputation, including instances of community action or resilience (e.g., Punch Line was rallied to be saved from closing in 2019).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A venue's reputation among comedians, politicians, and patrons, and stories of community efforts to preserve it, are cited as evidence of cultural importance and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nurturing environment / ability to develop talent
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the club is known for 'nurturing' performers and helping turn them into world‑famous comedians ('known for its nurturing environment and its ability to turn performers into world-famous comedians').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs that regularly showcase or cultivate emerging talent (and have a track record of alumni success) are highlighted as desirable destinations both for audiences and aspiring comedians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational/training programs and schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of workshops, classes, or formal schools connected to the venue (e.g., The Groundlings 'is a school that teaches the art of improvisation', BATS School of Improv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Venues that offer multi-session classes, workshops, or formal training are valued for their role in developing performers and providing participatory opportunities for those wanting to learn improv or sketch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming variety and curation
rubrics_metrics.description: The mix and curation of shows (e.g., 'a wide range of comedic offerings—from big names to up and coming performers', 'five to six hand-picked comedians', variety of joke styles in one evening).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A curated lineup, diversity of performers, and blend of established and emerging acts are presented positively; the page notes evening formats that include multiple, different-style comedians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show frequency, duration, and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule regularity and show structure (e.g., Cheaper Than Therapy runs shows Thursday–Sunday; shows last about 70–90 minutes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequent, reliably scheduled shows and clear show lengths/format are useful for planning visits; the article cites regular weekly schedules and typical run times as helpful details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue type and comedic focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the venue emphasizes stand-up, improv, sketch, or functions as a theater/company (e.g., The Groundlings = sketch/improv workshop, BATS = improvised shows & theater company).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different venues cater to different tastes — improv-focused companies vs traditional stand-up clubs vs sketch theaters — and the page distinguishes them to guide audience expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location / neighborhood prestige and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographic placement and neighborhood (e.g., 'Situated along the famous Sunset Strip', locations listed for each club).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A club's placement in well-known entertainment districts (Sunset Strip, Fort Mason, Fisherman’s Wharf) is treated as a plus for atmosphere, accessibility, and cultural cachet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amenities and on-site offerings (food, bar, seating)
rubrics_metrics.description: On-site amenities like food, drink, and seating comfort (e.g., Cobb’s offers 400 seats and food 'and a huckleberry twist'; Flappers is 'Comedy Club and Restaurant').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs that combine dining or comfortable seating with shows are depicted as offering a fuller night out; capacity and menu offerings can influence the experience and are mentioned as practical considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special events and draw nights
rubrics_metrics.description: Unique recurring events that attract visitors (e.g., Flappers' 'Celebrity Drop-In Tuesdays' where famous comedians drop in).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular special-event nights or celebrity drop-ins are highlighted as high-value experiences and reasons to time a visit; they increase a club's appeal beyond standard shows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intimacy and audience experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of intimacy and the type of audience experience (e.g., Cheaper Than Therapy is described as 'an intimate venue' with energetic shows featuring different joke styles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smaller, intimate venues are presented as delivering close-up, lively experiences with emerging talent, while larger venues may emphasize big-name acts and capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resilience and adaptability
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability of a venue to survive challenges and adapt (e.g., Cobb’s survived fires and relocations; Punch Line faced closing due to rent increases but was saved).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories of resilience (relocation after fire, community efforts to prevent closure) are used to indicate a venue's staying power and continued relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ease of booking / ticketing encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical guidance to book or reserve (e.g., 'But don’t settle for watching the shows online, nothing beats seeing it live—get booking!', 'reserve a table on “Celebrity Drop-In Tuesdays.”').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page encourages purchasing tickets or reserving tables for popular nights; accessibility of booking and reservation options is treated as part of the visitor experience.
